text: 22.4 L of any gas at STP contains:
explanation: 22.4L = 1 mole molecules. Atoms = moles × atomicity. Atomicity varies per gas.
trick: 22.4L = 1 mole molecules. But atoms depend on atomicity of the specific gas!

trick: H₂O=bent(104.5°), NH₃=trigonal pyramidal(107°), CH₄=tetrahedral(109.5°).

text: At constant T, pressure doubled. Volume:
explanation: Boyle's Law: PV = constant. 2P × V/2 = PV.
trick: Boyle: P↑ V↓. Charles: T↑ V↑. Gay-Lussac: T↑ P↑.

text: ΔH<0 and ΔS<0. Reaction is spontaneous:
explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. At low T, TΔS small → ΔG negative → spontaneous.
trick: ΔH− ΔS− → low T. ΔH+ ΔS+ → high T. Use ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.

trick: High P → fewer moles side. Haber process uses this.

trick: SHE = 0V. +E° = better oxidizing agent. -E° = better reducing agent.

text: Half-life of first order reaction is independent of:
explanation: t½ = 0.693/k. Depends on k but NOT on initial concentration.
trick: First order: t½ = 0.693/k (concentration independent). Zero order: t½ depends on [A₀].

explanation: Nuclear charge increases → stronger pull on electrons → higher EN.
trick: Period: EN left→right increases. Group: EN top→bottom decreases. Most EN: F.

text: Heavy water (D₂O) differs from H₂O in:
explanation: Higher density, BP, MP. Chemical reactions slightly slower.
trick: D₂O heavier → denser, higher BP/MP. Toxic to biological systems.

text: Which alkali metal reacts most vigorously with water?
explanation: Reactivity: Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs. Ionization energy decreases down group.
trick: Cs most reactive. Li floats, Na fizzes, K catches fire, Cs/Rb explode.

explanation: Acid strength ∝ 1/(H-X bond strength). Bond strength F>Cl>Br>I. So HI > HBr > HCl > HF.
trick: HI strongest acid. HF weakest acid but strongest bond. Electronegativity ≠ acid strength.

text: Transition metal with highest melting point:
explanation: Tungsten: MP = 3422°C. Highest of all metals. Maximum d-electron contribution to bonding.
trick: W = highest MP. Used in bulb filaments. W = Tough = Temperature-resistant.

trick: Ligands first (alphabetical) then metal with Roman numeral. Ammine has 2 m's.

trick: 1C=meth, 2C=eth, 3C=prop, 4C=but. Alcohol=-ol. Aldehyde=-al. Ketone=-one.

trick: Carbocation stability: 3°>2°>1°>methyl. Carbanion: reverse. Radical: 3°>2°>1°.

trick: SN2 = backside = inversion. SN1 = carbocation = racemization. 3° prefers SN1.

trick: 3°→immediate, 2°→5 min, 1°→no reaction. Turbidity = alkyl chloride formation.

text: Test that distinguishes aldehydes from ketones:
explanation: Tollens (ammoniacal AgNO₃) → silver mirror with aldehydes only.
trick: Tollens=silver mirror=aldehyde. Iodoform=CHI₃=CH₃CO- group.

trick: BOD high = polluted. BOD low = clean. Fish die when BOD > 8 ppm.

text: Elevation of boiling point is a _________ property:
explanation: Colligative properties depend on number of solute particles, not their nature: ΔTb, ΔTf, osmotic pressure, relative lowering of VP.
trick: 4 colligative properties: ΔTb, ΔTf, osmotic pressure, relative lowering of VP. All depend on number of particles.

explanation: Catalyst provides alternative pathway with lower activation energy. Does NOT change equilibrium position or ΔH of reaction.
trick: Catalyst: lower Ea → faster reaction. Doesn't change Keq or ΔH. Appears in stoichiometry but regenerated.

text: Which gas is responsible for acid rain?
explanation: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃. NO₂ + H₂O → HNO₃. These cause acid rain (pH < 5.6).
trick: Acid rain: SO₂ + NO₂ from burning fossil fuels. CO₂ causes global warming, not acid rain directly.
